recent_articles.title: Monsoon keeps India waiting, but brutal rain and hail to crash the party Monday - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** southwest monsoon is experiencing a slight delay in its official onset, but active weather systems are causing heavy rain, thundersqualls, and hailstorms across multiple states. The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts widespread atmospheric activity for Monday, June 1st, with downpours targeting the south peninsular region, while isolated heavy rainfall is expected for Kerala, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, and South Interior Karnataka.  The northeastern states of Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura are also on alert for isolated heavy showers.

recent_articles.title: SIR enumeration phase begins in Odisha, Mizoram, Sikkim and Manipur, says EC | Today News
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** of India has commenced the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Odisha, Mizoram, Sikkim, and Manipur. The enumeration process involves Booth Level Officers (BLOs) visiting homes to collect and verify voter registration forms. Voters can submit their completed forms through BLOs or online.  Eligible voters must submit their forms by June 28th for inclusion in the draft electoral rolls. The **Election Commission** emphasizes that the SIR exercise aims to ensure accurate and comprehensive voter lists, including all eligible citizens aged 18 and above while removing ineligible individuals.

recent_articles.title: Phase 3 of SIR exercise begins in Odisha, Manipur, Sikkim, Mizoram - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission** initiated phase 3 of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in **Odisha**, **Mizoram**, **Sikkim**, and **Manipur**.  Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will conduct house-to-house visits to distribute, collect, and verify enumeration forms. Electors can submit their forms online or through BLOs. The deadline for submitting forms is June 28th, after which eligible voters can apply for registration as a new voter. **The four states** involved account for over 3.67 crore electors.

recent_articles.title: BJP Core Group Meet At PM Modi's Residence Today, Rajya Sabha Polls On Agenda
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** top leaders, including Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, JP Nadda, and party president Nitin Nabin, will meet at **Prime Minister Narendra Modi's** residence this evening to discuss the upcoming Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections. The meeting will focus on finalizing candidates for these elections, which are scheduled for June 18th, as well as strategizing for the high-stakes Rajya Sabha polls following the recent defeat of the Women's reservation bill.  The party also plans to discuss strengthening its organization, mobilizing supporters, and highlighting achievements of the Modi government over the past twelve years.

recent_articles.title: Who drinks the most? Arunachal tops national chart, Himachal leads North - The Tribune
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)-6** revealed that **Arunachal Pradesh** has the highest proportion of men aged 15 and above reporting alcohol consumption, at 50.5 percent.  In northern India, **Himachal Pradesh** leads in alcohol consumption among men with 30.2 percent reporting consumption. The survey also found that **Chandigarh** has the highest overweight or obese population among men, with 48.5 percent of men falling into this category.

recent_articles.title: New worm-eating snake named after Mizoram herpetologist - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Scientists** from **Mizoram University** and the Max Planck Institute for Biology have described a new species of snake, **Trachischium lalremsangai**, found in the jungles of Mizoram and Myanmar. The snake, named after Hmar Tlawmte Lalremsanga, was identified based on two specimens collected in Murlen National Park and Haka Township.  The researchers noted that this species is distinct from other members of its genus due to its light-brown belly and unique scales behind the eye.

recent_articles.title: Assam filmmaker’s documentary screened at British Film Institute in London - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chalo India with Ericji (Varanasi)**, a documentary by Assam filmmaker Rajdeep Choudhury, was screened at the British Film Institute in London. The film, part of a larger travel and cultural anthology presented by former UK MP **Eric Ollerenshaw**, explores Varanasi's culture, history, and everyday life during Makar Sankranti.  The screening was organized by the High Commission of India, London, in collaboration with the U.K. Asian Film Festival and Tongues on Fire. The documentary team received the Heritage Cinema Excellence Award for their contributions to cultural storytelling through cinema.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: Rise in cybercrime but overall crime rate dropped in 2024, says latest NCRB report - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)** reported a 6% decline in overall crime in India for 2024, but cybercrime cases surged by over 17%.  **NCRB** data revealed that fraud constituted the majority of cybercrime cases, followed by sexual exploitation and extortion. The report also highlighted a rise in crimes against the state, with **The Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act** being the most frequently cited law. Suicide rates increased significantly in 2024, particularly among agricultural workers, unemployed individuals, daily wage laborers, and students.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Why is India turning to crocodiles and snakes to ‘fence’ Bangladesh border? | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Indian** Border Security Force (BSF) is exploring the use of apex predators like crocodiles and venomous snakes to deter undocumented migration along its border with **Bangladesh**.  This controversial plan, aimed at addressing challenging terrain that makes traditional fencing difficult, has raised concerns from human rights activists and wildlife conservationists. The BSF's directive to explore this option comes despite the fact that these animals are not native to the region and could pose a threat to local ecosystems and communities. Critics argue that deploying such measures is inhumane and ineffective, highlighting the government's use of fear tactics against undocumented migrants. This approach has been compared to similar controversial strategies employed in the United States, including proposals for using alligators or snakes to deter migrants.

recent_articles.title: Israel airlifts 240 Bnei Menashe members from Mizoram as India maintains security advisory - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Government of India** issued an advisory regarding the security situation in Israel amidst the ongoing war in West Asia.  **Israel** airlifted approximately 240 individuals from Mizoram to Tel Aviv as part of **Operation Wings of Dawn**, a program sanctioned by **Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu**. This operation marks the first time such a large number of members of the Bnei Menashe community have been airlifted to Israel during a period of regional conflict.

recent_articles.title: Earth Day 2026: How Nature walks, parks, and trails are sparking a new conservation movement - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rohit Girotra**, co-founder of the Bangalore Butterfly Club (BBC), has seen a surge in interest in butterflies and butterfly-focused activities. The BBC, which began in 2012, now boasts nearly 600 members and offers guided walks at Doresanipalya Forest Research Station.  **Ashok Sengupta**, another BBC co-founder, believes that butterfly watching is an easy portal into the natural world for children. **Isaac Kehimkar**, a naturalist and photographer, has documented over 40 Facebook groups dedicated to butterflies worldwide. These groups have helped raise awareness of these insects through social media and mobile cameras. Butterfly parks and trails are also becoming increasingly popular across India, with locations like Sammilan Shetty's Butterfly Park in Karnataka offering educational programs on butterfly conservation.

recent_articles.title: Five deaths, no arrests as fresh violence grips Manipur - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Since April 7th, **Manipur** has experienced five killings, including the deaths of two children. The **National Investigation Agency (NIA)** is investigating the April 7th attack on a family in Tronglaobi, Bishnupur, but roadblocks have hindered their progress.  The attacks have led to clashes between locals and security forces demanding arrests. **Meitei** civil society groups have accused **Kuki-Zo insurgent groups** of being behind the violence, while the Deputy Chief Minister of Manipur, **Losii Dikho**, believes these incidents could be an attempt to incite unrest.

recent_articles.title: Door-to-door visit by Census enumerators in eight States/U.T.s from April 16 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** announced the commencement of door-to-door enumeration for the first phase of the 2027 Population Census, known as the House Listing and Housing Operations (HLO). Beginning on April 16th in eight states and union territories including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, and Delhi's NDMC area and Cantonment Board, enumerators will collect data for the HLO phase. This follows a 15-day self-enumeration period.

recent_articles.title: Constitution Amendment Bill proposes possible change in size of State Assemblies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Constitution** (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes significant changes to State Legislative Assemblies by restarting the delimitation process and removing a long-standing constitutional freeze on seat readjustments. The bill aims to update constituency boundaries based on population changes and will be introduced in a Special Session of Parliament beginning April 16th.  The Delimitation Commission, chaired by a former or sitting Supreme Court judge, will determine the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and redraw parliamentary and Assembly constituencies. Public consultation on draft proposals will precede finalization before the new boundaries take effect for elections after the Commission's final orders are published in the Gazette of India.

recent_articles.title: Meghalaya yields new burrowing reed snake - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A team of researchers from multiple institutions, including **Help Earth**, **Cotton University**, and the **Zoological Survey of India**, have described a new species of burrowing reed snake called *Calamaria garoensis* found in Meghalaya's West Garo Hills district. The study, published in Taprobanica, confirmed that this species is distinct from other related species based on morphological examination and mitochondrial DNA analysis.  The discovery highlights the rich biodiversity of the region and emphasizes the need for further research and conservation efforts to protect these often overlooked creatures.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Self-enumeration facility availed by 5.72 lakh households so far in first phase - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Registrar General of India (RGI)** announced that over 5.72 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the first phase of the Census 2027. This digital initiative reflects growing participation in the census, with a special portal available for citizens in specific areas including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Sikkim, Odisha, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, and Delhi's NDMC and Cantonment Board. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their details online, facilitating a faster and more convenient contribution to nation-building.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI may roll out SIR in remaining 17 States, 5 UTs post polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** is considering rolling out the third and final phase of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for voters' lists in 22 states and Union territories after the Assembly elections this month. The exercise, which aims to clean up electoral rolls, could begin after the polls conclude on April 29th or after the declaration of results.  The **Election Commission** has already conducted SIR in 10 states and three Union Territories, covering nearly 60 crore voters.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Polls 2026: LDF, UDF and NDA in a no-holds barred battle for supremacy in south Kerala - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming Kerala Assembly elections are shaping up to be a three-way battle between the ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF), the Opposition United Democratic Front (UDF), and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).  **V. Sivankutty**, **Rajeev Chandrasekhar**, and **K. S. Sabarinadhan** are among the prominent figures in this race, with each party vying for control of key constituencies. The LDF and UDF are facing challenges from the NDA's growing influence, particularly in Thiruvananthapuram.  The outcome of these elections will likely depend on how voters navigate complex political alliances and the impact of issues like the Sabarimala gold theft case.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027 kicks off: How to do self-enumeration: step-by-step guide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner will conduct the 2027 census, a massive administrative and statistical exercise that collects demographic data on the entire country. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their household information online before enumerators visit, offering flexibility in filling out the census schedule.  The dates for self-enumeration vary by state and union territory, with most starting in April 2026. Census data is expected to be published within 2027 due to the digital nature of the process.

recent_articles.title: 55,000 households use Census self-enumeration portal on day one - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Droupadi Murmu**, **Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan**, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** were among the first to use the online self-enumeration portal for the 2027 Population Census in eight States and Union Territories. The portal, which launched on April 1, 2026, allows households to provide information about their housing conditions and assets before enumerators visit.  The first phase of the census, focusing on house listing operations and housing census (HLO), will run until May 15th in these areas. Data collected through self-enumeration is confidential and will be used for evidence-based planning and policy formulation.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: India begins counting a billion-plus people in mega exercise
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** is launching its largest census in over 15 years, with a goal of capturing demographic and socioeconomic data on its more than 1.4 billion people. The two-phase exercise will involve over three million officials collecting information on housing conditions, household assets, education, migration, and fertility.  The census will also include caste data, marking a significant shift in focus from basic demographics to broader socio-economic indicators. This comprehensive data collection is crucial for policymaking, welfare delivery, and political representation as India's population continues to evolve.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Not a good precedent for Governors to contest elections immediately after office, says Sreedharan Pillai - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Former Governor** of Mizoram and Goa, **[Name Redacted]**, has chosen not to contest the Chengannur Assembly constituency despite strong community support. He believes it would set a precedent for Governors entering electoral politics immediately after demitting office. The former governor also expressed his preference for remaining independent due to the absence of a pension for Governors.  **[Name Redacted]** acknowledges allegations of a covert understanding between the CPI(M) and BJP, but maintains that past political realities contradict such claims. He believes the BJP-led NDA is well positioned for a strong performance in the upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Prof. N.V.R. Jyoti Kumar becomes new Vice-Chancellor of Sri Krishnadevaraya University - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prof. N.V.R. Jyoti Kumar**, Senior Professor at **Mizoram University**, assumed the role of Vice-Chancellor at **Sri Krishnadevaraya University** on March 28, 2026.  He began his tenure by garlanding statues of Jyotirao Phule and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar before meeting with staff members from various departments and positions. He emphasized the importance of student welfare and the need for strong leadership within the university.
